title: Early signs of AI-driven productivity growth in the information sector
gist: A St. Louis Fed FRED blog shows information-sector labor productivity grew 13.70% from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026 versus 2.17% for the whole economy, possibly an early sign of GenAI-driven productivity gains.

insights.claim: From Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, US information-sector labor productivity grew 13.70% while aggregate labor productivity grew 2.17%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: The gap between sector and aggregate productivity is the strongest data hint so far that GenAI is showing up in measured output.

insights.claim: From 2010 to 2026 information-sector labor productivity grew an average 7.68% a year versus 1.22% for the aggregate economy, so the sector normally leads but the recent gap is unusually large.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Baseline matters: the sector's outperformance is normal, so look for acceleration relative to that trend.

insights.claim: The authors say it is possible these are early signs of AI-driven productivity gains, noting the information sector (publishing, broadcasting, telecom, data processing and data centres) is only 1.8% of employment but has historically contributed strongly to aggregate growth.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Evidence is suggestive and sector-narrow; monitor whether the gains spread to other industries.

insights.claim: The analysis starts in Q1 2024 deliberately, when GenAI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Claude were gaining mainstream use.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: The chosen start date shapes the comparison; it is a timing association, not proof of causation.
